items.title: Close the --seed non-finite determinism hole in pick()
items.acceptance: --seed Infinity and --seed -Infinity each return the identical aphorism on every run at exit 0, with the same filters applied
items.notes: CONDUCTOR-CONFIRMED defect (kickoff probe: 6 distinct aphorisms in 6 runs, exit 0). Resolution chosen: DETERMINISTIC PICK, not exit 2. Reasoning, judged against the SPEC's own rules: args.js already accepts Infinity as numeric (Number('Infinity') is not NaN) and the Domain rule promises determinism for --seed with no finiteness carve-out, so rejecting it would mean inventing a NEW undocumented validation rule rather than fixing the actual defect — which is that select.js gates its deterministic branch on Number.isFinite while toUint32Seed's IEEE-754 bit-fold already handles +/-Infinity deterministically. NaN stays exit 2 (parseSeedValue already rejects it) and that is correct and unchanged. Doc statement of this resolution belongs to I-3, which is why this item's files_hint is code+test only. NOT flagged route_class core despite playbook L-026: the allocator posture is trickle with allow_premium_pct 0 and opus at 96%, and gear 1's rule is S-effort sonnet builds — deliberately routing a 3-line fix to fable would spend premium the allocator has explicitly zeroed. || VERIFIED cycle 3 by the conductor with checks authored at verification time (the builder never saw them): full test_cmd 52/52 green, end-to-end CLI stability 1-distinct-of-8 for +Inf, -Inf, and +Inf under a --tag filter, and a discriminator that independently re-derived the expected corpus index for each seed (a degenerate index-pin would have passed the stability check alone). NaN contract and the unseeded random branch both confirmed unchanged. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-003-verify-I-1.txt

items.title: Mutation sweep of every documented behavior against the existing suite
items.acceptance: every documented flag and Domain-rule behavior has been mutated at least once against the current suite, and each surviving mutant is recorded with the exact mutation applied and the suite's response
items.notes: MEASUREMENT, not reading (playbook L-031). Behaviors to mutate: seed determinism, unseeded selection, --author case-insensitive matching, --tag membership matching, author+tag AND intersection, empty-set error contract, --list completeness and corpus order, --json single-line shape, the three exit codes, HELP content. Produces a survivor list ONLY. The HOLE-vs-BOUNDARY classification (L-033) is the CONDUCTOR's judgment and is deliberately withheld from this item: a survivor at a genuinely indiscriminable point (unseeded uniformity is the expected example) is the check being correct, and 'hardening' it produces a test that false-rejects honest output. Scratch copies for mutation must be whole-repo-minus-.git, never a hand-enumerated file subset (L-030). || VERIFIED cycle 4 by the conductor. 27 mutants across every catalogued behavior; baseline 52/52. Agent reported 19 KILLED / 7 SURVIVED / 1 EQUIVALENT (M06-EQUIV, dropping .toLowerCase() on the tag ENTRY side, was a no-op because every corpus tag is already lowercase - correctly excluded and replaced by a query-side variant that killed). Conductor re-measurement re-derived all 7 survivors AND a 4-mutant control sample of claimed KILLS from the one-sentence descriptions only, never from the agent's diffs, each in its own whole-repo-minus-.git copy: 11/11 agree, and every survivor carries a conductor-authored observable-difference probe, so none is an equivalent mutant. Classification (conductor, per SPEC Domain rules): 5 HOLE (M07, M12, M13, M14, M21), 1 BOUNDARY (M22 - only the error-message wording changes; exit 2 + clean stdout + stderr message all still hold), 1 DEFERRED to I-3 (M16, --list --json, the surface SPEC lists as an OPEN AMBIGUITY - testing it now would promote today's implementation to a promise and pre-empt I-3). Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-004-verify-I-2a.txt, .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md, .swarm/runs/cycle-004-mutation-sweep.json

items.title: Close HOLE survivors in the CLI-level suite
items.acceptance: each behavior the conductor classified HOLE is covered by a test that fails against its specific mutation, and whose removal lets that same mutation survive
items.notes: Admits tests ONLY for survivors the conductor classified HOLE — never for a surface that merely looks untested. Each test must be proven twice (L-029): failable against its mutation AND attributable, i.e. removing it lets the mutation survive. Planning-time hypotheses, to be settled by I-2a's actual measurement and not assumed: the current --list test asserts only a line-count floor and never order, and the current --json test uses JSON.parse after trim() so a pretty-printed multi-line mutant may still parse. || SETTLED by I-2a (cycle 4). Four assigned HOLE survivors, all observable through the shipped binary: M07 (--tag test must exit 1 - membership, not substring; the corpus has a 'testing' tag and no 'test' tag), M12 (--list line count must equal the corpus size - the existing assertion is a FLOOR of 40 against 50 entries, so dropping an entry passes), M13 (--list first/last line must match corpus order - nothing asserts order today), M14 (--json must be exactly one line - the existing test JSON.parses a trimmed blob, which a pretty-printed object also satisfies). Both planning-time hypotheses in this item were CONFIRMED by measurement. Exact mutations: .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md || VERIFIED cycle 5 by an independent conductor harness (.swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-I-2b.py, builder never saw it). All four HOLEs proven twice: FAILABLE (mutation applied, suite fails and the designated new test is named) and ATTRIBUTABLE in the strict form (mutation applied + all four new tests skipped -> 52 pass / 0 fail, exactly the pre-sweep baseline, so no pre-existing test was doing the work). A skip-sanity control confirms --test-skip-pattern does not disable the whole run. Suite 52 -> 56 green. Recorded overlap: M12 is length-changing, so it also trips the M13 order test; isolation of M12 alone still leaves fail=1 by design, not by defect.

items.title: Close remaining HOLE survivors in the pure-module suite
items.acceptance: each remaining conductor-classified HOLE survivor in the parser or selection layer is covered by a test that fails against its specific mutation and whose removal lets that mutation survive
items.notes: Same twice-proven rule as I-2b. Scoped to test/args.test.js so it shares no file with I-2b (test/cli.test.js) or I-1 (test/select.test.js) — pairwise-disjoint even though this run's waves are size 1. If I-2a's survivors land entirely in one file, this item is closed as not-needed rather than padded with tests to justify its existence. || SETTLED by I-2a (cycle 4). Exactly ONE assigned HOLE survivor, and it does live in the parser, so this item is neither padded nor closed as not-needed: M21 - parseSeedValue rejecting negative seeds survives the whole suite, i.e. parseArgs(['--seed','-5']) yielding seed === -5 with no error is unprotected. Turning a valid invocation into exit 2 contradicts the Domain rule that exit 2 means unknown flag or missing flag argument. M22 (the other args.js survivor) is classified BOUNDARY and must NOT be hardened. Details: .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md || CLOSED cycle 6. Two additive tests in test/args.test.js cover both argument forms ('--seed','-5') and ('--seed=-5'). Conductor harness .swarm/runs/cycle-006-verify-I-2c.py: FAILABLE (M21 -> fail=2, both failures named are the new tests), DENOMINATOR (pattern removes exactly 2 of 58, leaving the 56-test baseline green), ATTRIBUTABLE strict (M21 + new tests filtered -> tests=56 pass=56 fail=0, the pre-cycle baseline to the test), SKIP-SANITY (breaking control mutation under the same pattern -> 7 pre-existing failures). Product tree byte-identical to HEAD. M22 left unhardened as classified.

items.title: Settle the four doc/behaviour divergences identically in SPEC.md and README.md
items.acceptance: SPEC.md Domain rules and README.md state in matching wording: how --author matches, what --list does with --seed, what --list --json emits, and how a non-finite --seed behaves; and SPEC.md's OPEN AMBIGUITIES comment is gone rather than left open
items.notes: Four divergences, not three: the I-1 resolution is the fourth and is documented here rather than in I-1, keeping code and prose in separate file scopes. Documentation follows the SHIPPED behavior (--author is substring containment, case-insensitive) rather than changing behavior to match prose — changing the match semantics would be a user-visible behavior change, which the brief forbids. Depends on I-1 so the seed prose describes a resolution that has actually landed. || MEASURED EVIDENCE from I-2a (cycle 4) for divergence (c): mutant M16 rewrote --list --json from NDJSON to a single pretty-printed JSON array and the full 52-test suite stayed green, so that surface is completely unprotected today. It is deliberately NOT being hardened by I-2b/I-2c - no Domain rule describes the combination, so a test would freeze the current implementation and pre-empt this item. Settle the rule here first. || NEW measured evidence (cycle 5): the --list LINE FORMAT ("<text> — <author>", em dash, single line) is now pinned by the M13 order test but is stated by no Domain rule — the rules describe order and completeness of --list, never its rendering. Same shape of gap as M16: a test now enforces something the spec does not promise. I-3 should either write the rule or loosen the assertion to order-only. Do not silently leave the test as the de-facto spec.

items.title: Corpus attribution triage — risk-ranked list for a human
items.acceptance: a written risk-ranked list names the corpus entries most likely to carry a wrong or unverifiable attribution with a stated reason each, and no file in the repo describes the corpus as audited, verified, or fact-checked
items.notes: TRIAGE, never an audit — nothing here can be confirmed without sources this run cannot reach, and the deliverable is explicitly a list for a human to settle (KI-2, T-006). Rank by internally-observable risk signals only: folklore maxims historically credited to several different people, wording that looks paraphrased or compressed rather than verbatim, entries already hedged as Anonymous (lowest risk, already honest), and entries traceable to a specific well-documented publication (lower risk). The stress-test's demo-embarrassment lens put this ABOVE the test items in value: a programming-aphorism CLI with misattributed quotes fails in exactly the way a green suite cannot see.
